methods.name: Create
methods.description:
Create a new grant

 Creates a single grant that gives a principal access to a resource with a specific relation.
 This is the fundamental operation for establishing permissions.

methods.name: Delete
methods.description:
Delete a single grant by spec

 Removes an existing grant by matching the principal, resource, and relation.
 This is a surgical operation — it removes one specific grant without affecting others.

methods.name: BootstrapGrant
methods.description:
Bootstrap grant during resource creation

 Creates grants during resource creation when standard authorization cannot work yet
 because no tuples exist.

methods.name: CleanupResourceGrants
methods.description:
Clean up every grant naming a deleted resource.

 Removes all grants associated with a deleted resource.

methods.name: RevokeOrgAccess
methods.description:
Remove a person from an organization.

 Removes every role the identity account holds on the organization, then
 every grant it holds on the organization's resources: what was
 shared with it (agents, vaults, sessions and the rest) and its
 team memberships. From that moment it reaches nothing in the
 organization. What it created stays with the organization and is still
 recorded as its work; the authorization model admits a person to their
 own work only while they hold a role in the organization, so it becomes
 theirs again only if they are invited back. What was shared with them
 does not come back.

methods.name: BootstrapRevokeOrgAccess
methods.description:
Remove a person from an organization via the system (bootstrap) path.

 The system-flow twin of revokeOrgAccess: identical revocation behavior, but
 authorized by can_bootstrap_iam on platform:stigmer instead of
 can_grant_access on the organization.

methods.name: Get
methods.description:
Get a grant by its unique identifier.

 Returns the full grant including its principal, resource, and relation binding.

methods.name: CheckMyPermission
methods.description:
Check whether the AUTHENTICATED CALLER has a permission on a resource.

 This is the self-check RPC for clients (web console, desktop, SDKs):
 "Do I have permission Y on resource Z?"

 The principal is always derived server-side from the authenticated token.
 The input has no principal field by design — clients cannot name a
 principal, so cross-principal permission probing is structurally
 impossible (the Kubernetes SelfSubjectAccessReview pattern).

 Use Cases:
 - Pre-flight UI checks before showing buttons/actions
 - Permission-gated rendering (PermissionGate components)

 Input: CheckMyPermissionInput with resource, relation, and optional contextual grants
 Output: CheckAuthorizationResult with is_authorized boolean

methods.name: CheckAuthorization
methods.description:
Check if a principal is authorized to perform a relation on a resource

 This is the fundamental authorization check RPC that answers the question:
 "Does principal X have permission Y on resource Z?"

 It provides a simple boolean answer based on the complete authorization state,
 including existing grants, inherited permissions, and group memberships.

 This RPC is an INTERNAL-FACING contract for the platform's own
 authorization pipeline (service-to-service and in-process checks).
 Client-facing self checks must use checkMyPermission instead.

 Use Cases:
 - API request authorization before processing operations
 - Service-to-service authorization
 - Team-based access checks

 Input: CheckAuthorizationInput with grant spec and optional contextual grants
 Output: CheckAuthorizationResult with is_authorized boolean

methods.name: ListAuthorizedResourceIds
methods.description:
List all resource IDs of a specific kind that a principal is authorized to access

 This RPC answers: "What are all the [resource-kind] that [principal] can [relation] on?"
 Essential for building permission-aware UIs and filtering resource lists.

 Use Cases:
 - Resource list filtering in dropdowns
 - Permission-based navigation
 - Bulk authorization checks

 Input: ListAuthorizedResourceIdsInput with principal, resource_kind, and relation
 Output: AuthorizedResourceIdsList containing all accessible resource IDs

methods.name: ListAuthorizedPrincipalIds
methods.description:
List all principal IDs of a specific kind that are authorized to access a resource

 This RPC answers: "What are all the [principal-kind] that have [relation] access on [resource]?"
 Inverse of listAuthorizedResourceIds.

 Use Cases:
 - Resource access audit (who can access this?)
 - Team discovery for resources
 - Compliance and security audits

 Input: ListAuthorizedPrincipalIdsInput with resource, principal_kind, and relation
 Output: AuthorizedPrincipalIdsList containing all authorized principal IDs

methods.name: ListResourceAccessByPrincipal
methods.description:
List all principals and their roles on a resource, grouped by principal.

 This RPC answers: "Who has access to this resource, and what roles do they have?"
 Returns each principal with full display information and all their role grants,
 optionally including roles inherited from parent resources.

 Use Cases:
 - Organization members page (show all users and their roles)
 - Resource "Share" dialog (show who already has access)
 - Access audit views

 Input: ListResourceAccessInput with resource ref and include_inherited flag
 Output: ResourceAccessByPrincipalList with PrincipalAccess entries

methods.name: GetPrincipalResourceRoles
methods.description:
Get all roles a specific principal has on a specific resource.

 This RPC answers: "What roles does [principal] have on [resource]?"
 Returns role metadata (code, display name, description) for each assigned role.

 Use Cases:
 - Displaying a user's current role in a resource detail view
 - Pre-populating role selectors when editing access
 - Permission summary for a specific user-resource pair

 Input: PrincipalResourceInput with principal and resource refs
 Output: PrincipalResourceRoles with list of RoleInfo entries

methods.name: GetPrincipalsCount
methods.description:
Count distinct principals that have access to a resource.

 This RPC answers: "How many [principal-kind] have access to this organization?"
 Used for member count badges and summary statistics.

 Use Cases:
 - Organization members count badge in navigation
 - Settings page member summary

 Input: GetPrincipalsCountInput with org and principal_kind
 Output: PrincipalsCount with integer count

methods.name: ListAccessHistory
methods.description:
List an organization's access history: every time someone was given
 or lost access to the organization or to a resource in it, who did it,
 why, and when.

 Without after_sequence the entries come newest first, for people
 reading what happened lately. With after_sequence they come oldest
 first, starting just after that entry, for a tool that keeps its own
 copy: it asks for what came after the last entry it holds. Each
 organization numbers its entries from 1 in the order they happened,
 with no gaps above the oldest kept entry, so a reader that resumes
 after entry N never misses one the server still keeps.

 A server may keep the history for a limited time, set by its operator.
 It then removes the oldest entries first and never reuses a number:
 every page says how many days the server keeps the history
 (retention_days, 0 for good) and the oldest number it still holds
 (oldest_sequence), so a tool can tell entries that were removed from
 entries it missed.

 Only the organization's owners and administrators may read it, and a
 parent organization's administrators for a child, since they are
 administrators in every child. Whoever may read it reads all of it. The
 Enterprise and
 Cloud editions keep the history; an open-source server keeps none and
 answers UNIMPLEMENTED. A host may refuse the read for its own reasons,
 such as a plan that does not include it.

methodTypes.name: GrantSpec
methodTypes.description:
GrantSpec defines the desired state of a grant binding.
 It specifies WHO (principal) gets WHAT permission (relation) on WHICH resource.

fields.name: Principal
fields.description:
Principal: WHO is being granted access
 This can be any API resource that acts as an identity:
 - identity_account (individual user)
 - team (group of users)
 - organization (for cross-org grants)
 - Any other resource that can be a subject in authorization

fields.name: Resource
fields.description:
Resource: WHAT is being accessed
 This can be any API resource that is being protected:
 - organization
 - vault
 - cloud_resource (VPC, S3 bucket, etc.)
 - service
 - Any other resource that requires access control

fields.name: Relation
fields.description:
The permission being granted (e.g., "admin", "viewer", "owner").
 Maps to a role_code from ai.stigmer.iam.v1.IamRole.
 Examples: "admin", "editor", "viewer", "owner", "member"

methodTypes.name: ApiResourceRef
methodTypes.description:
ApiResourceRef represents a reference to ANY API resource in the system.
 It is intentionally generic and reusable for both principals and resources
 to maintain symmetry and flexibility in the authorization model.

 This message contains ONLY identification fields (kind, id, relation).
 For view/query responses that need display information, use ApiResourceRefView in io.proto.

fields.name: Kind
fields.description:
Type of the API resource being referenced
 This should be the resource kind as defined in ApiResourceKind enum.
 Examples: "identity_account", "team", "organization", "vault",
 "cloud_resource", "service", etc.

fields.name: Id
fields.description:
Unique identifier of the resource
 This is the resource's ID field (e.g., ida_01hqu..., tm_01hqt...). For an
 organization a request may give its slug instead; the server stores the
 id.

fields.name: Relation
fields.description:
Optional relation qualifier for the resource reference.
 Used when the reference needs additional context about the relationship.

 Primary use case: For team principals, this specifies the relation of the
 user to the team (e.g., "member", "admin").
 Example: principal { kind: "team", id: "tm-123", relation: "member" }
 means "members of team tm-123"

 This field qualifies HOW the principal relates to this resource reference,
 NOT the permission being granted (that's GrantSpec.relation).

methodTypes.name: RevokeOrgAccessInput
methodTypes.description: RevokeOrgAccessInput defines the input for revoking all of a user's access to an organization.

fields.name: IdentityAccountId
fields.description: The identity account whose access is being revoked

fields.name: Org
fields.description: The organization from which access is being revoked

methodTypes.name: CheckMyPermissionInput
methodTypes.description:
CheckMyPermissionInput defines input for checking whether the AUTHENTICATED
 CALLER has a permission on a resource.

 Unlike CheckAuthorizationInput, there is deliberately NO principal field:
 the principal is always derived server-side from the authenticated token —
 the only trustworthy source of caller identity. Clients cannot probe another
 user's permissions because the API gives them no way to name a principal.

 This mirrors the industry-standard self-check pattern (e.g. Kubernetes
 SelfSubjectAccessReview): self checks and cross-principal checks are
 separate API surfaces with separate trust models.

fields.name: Resource
fields.description: The resource being accessed (WHAT)

fields.name: Relation
fields.description: The permission to check (e.g., "can_edit", "can_grant_access").

fields.name: ContextualGrants
fields.description: Optional contextual grants for "what-if" scenarios

methodTypes.name: CheckAuthorizationResult
methodTypes.description: CheckAuthorizationResult contains the result of an authorization check.

fields.name: IsAuthorized
fields.description: Whether the principal is authorized

methodTypes.name: CheckAuthorizationInput
methodTypes.description: CheckAuthorizationInput defines input for checking if a principal is authorized.

fields.name: Grant
fields.description: The grant to check (principal, resource, relation)

fields.name: ContextualGrants
fields.description: Optional contextual grants for "what-if" scenarios

methodTypes.name: ListAuthorizedResourceIdsInput
methodTypes.description: ListAuthorizedResourceIdsInput defines input for listing resources a principal can access.

fields.name: Principal
fields.description: The principal whose access is being queried

fields.name: ResourceKind
fields.description: The kind of resources to check

fields.name: Relation
fields.description: The relation/permission to check for

fields.name: ContextualGrants
fields.description: Optional contextual grants for "what-if" scenarios

methodTypes.name: AuthorizedResourceIdsList
methodTypes.description: AuthorizedResourceIdsList contains all resource IDs a principal can access.

fields.name: ResourceIds
fields.description: Resource IDs the principal is authorized to access.

methodTypes.name: ListAuthorizedPrincipalIdsInput
methodTypes.description: ListAuthorizedPrincipalIdsInput defines input for listing principals that can access a resource.

fields.name: Resource
fields.description: The resource whose access is being queried

fields.name: PrincipalKind
fields.description: The kind of principals to check for

fields.name: Relation
fields.description: The relation/permission to check for

fields.name: ContextualGrants
fields.description: Optional contextual grants for "what-if" scenarios

methodTypes.name: AuthorizedPrincipalIdsList
methodTypes.description: AuthorizedPrincipalIdsList contains all principal IDs that can access a resource.

fields.name: PrincipalIds
fields.description: Principal IDs authorized to access the resource.

methodTypes.name: ListResourceAccessInput
methodTypes.description: ListResourceAccessInput defines input for querying access grants on a resource.

fields.name: Resource
fields.description: The resource to query access for

fields.name: IncludeInherited
fields.description: Whether to include inherited permissions from parent resources

methodTypes.name: ResourceAccessByPrincipalList
methodTypes.description:
ResourceAccessByPrincipalList groups access grants by principal, showing each
 principal and all their assigned roles on the queried resource.

fields.name: Entries
fields.description: Principal access entries.

methodTypes.name: PrincipalResourceInput
methodTypes.description: PrincipalResourceInput defines a generic input for operations involving a principal and a resource.

fields.name: Principal
fields.description: The principal in the relationship (WHO)

fields.name: Resource
fields.description: The resource in the relationship (WHAT)

methodTypes.name: PrincipalResourceRoles
methodTypes.description: PrincipalResourceRoles contains all roles a principal has on a specific resource.

fields.name: Roles
fields.description: Roles assigned to the principal on this resource.

methodTypes.name: GetPrincipalsCountInput
methodTypes.description: GetPrincipalsCountInput defines input for counting principals in an organization.

fields.name: Org
fields.description: Organization ID to count principals for

fields.name: PrincipalKind
fields.description: The kind of principals to count (identity_account or team)

methodTypes.name: PrincipalsCount
methodTypes.description: PrincipalsCount contains the count of principals.

fields.name: Count
fields.description: Number of principals matching the query.

methodTypes.name: ListAccessHistoryInput
methodTypes.description:
ListAccessHistoryInput names the organization whose access history to
 read, and where to start.

fields.name: Org
fields.description: The organization, by slug or id.

fields.name: PageSize
fields.description:
The most entries to return: 0 asks for the default page of 50, and a
 size above 100 is read as 100. A history only grows, so there is no size
 that returns every entry at once: follow next_page_token.

fields.name: PageToken
fields.description: The previous response's next_page_token, to continue that read.

fields.name: AfterSequence
fields.description:
Read oldest first, starting just after this entry's sequence; 0 reads
 from the oldest entry the server still keeps. Unset reads newest first.
 A tool that keeps its own copy passes the last sequence it holds.

methodTypes.name: AccessHistoryPage
methodTypes.description: AccessHistoryPage is one page of an organization's access history.

fields.name: Entries
fields.description:
The entries, newest first, or oldest first when the request named
 after_sequence.

fields.name: NextPageToken
fields.description:
Set when more entries may follow: pass it as page_token, with the same
 request otherwise, to continue. Empty when this page reached the end.
 A page may be short, even empty, and still carry a token.

fields.name: OldestSequence
fields.description:
The lowest sequence the organization's history still holds. When it
 holds none because every entry was removed, the sequence its next entry
 will get (one past the last it held); 0 only when it never held one. A
 server that keeps the history for a limited time removes
 the oldest entries first, so an organization's kept entries are always
 one unbroken run ending at its newest. A tool that asked for what came
 after N and reads an oldest_sequence above N + 1 knows that N + 1 to
 oldest_sequence - 1 were removed by retention, not missed. Whoever may
 read the history reads all of it, so the numbers have no other gaps.

fields.name: RetentionDays
fields.description:
How many days this server keeps the access history, 0 when it removes
 nothing. Entries older than this are removed.

enumTypes.name: ApiResourceVisibility
enumTypes.description:
Visibility controls who can access an API resource.
 This is orthogonal to ownership - visibility is about access control,
 while ownership (org) determines who manages the resource.

 Key distinction:
 - Ownership: Which organization controls/manages the resource
 - Visibility: Who can access/use the resource

 All resources belong to an organization. Visibility determines which
 users, inside that organization or in its child organizations, can read
 the resource. No level reaches every
 account on the server.

 The visibility levels map to FGA tuples:
 - PRIVATE: no additional viewer tuples (owner-only access)
 - ORG: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer tuple (everyone in the
   org — the org role hierarchy flows downward, so owners, admins, members
   AND read-only viewers all satisfy the organization#viewer userset)
 - CHILD_ORGS: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer
   (everyone in every child organization of the owning organization)

values.name: visibility_private
values.description:
Only the owner, explicitly granted principals, and — for blueprint kinds
 in the cloud edition — org admins can access.
 This is the default for personal and run-scoped resources.

 Org admins count as owners of blueprint kinds (agent, channel,
 skill, plugin), so a private blueprint stays
 manageable — and visible — to its org's admins. Personal kinds
 (sessions) stay creator-only.

values.name: visibility_org
values.description:
Everyone in the owning organization can access (read) this resource —
 all org roles including read-only viewers (the role just-in-time provisioning
 grants by default). Running or otherwise spending against the resource
 still requires the org-level member-or-guest permissions
 (can_create_session / can_create_run_in); org visibility widens
 read, never spend.

 FGA tuple: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer

values.name: visibility_child_orgs
values.description:
Everyone in every child organization of the owning organization can
 read and run this resource: the shared catalog an organization offers
 the organizations under it (spec.parent_org). Child organizations
 created later gain access automatically, and no other organization
 does. Instances, sessions, runs and vaults are never shared
 this way: each child runs the shared blueprint inside its own boundary.

 Only valid for blueprint kinds with supports_child_orgs: true, and only
 in an organization that is not itself a child.

 FGA tuple: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer

enumTypes.name: IdentityAccountProvisioningMode
enumTypes.description: IdentityAccountProvisioningMode defines how an identity account was created.

values.name: direct
values.description: User signed up directly via Stigmer's own authentication tenant.

values.name: federated
values.description: Account was created by the platform for federated authentication via a FederationIssuer.

values.name: app_user
values.description:
A person who signs in from an organization's own product: the
 product's backend asks for their token with TokenService.mintUserToken,
 and Stigmer signs it. The console calls them App users.

 The idp_id uses the composite encoding "stgm_pc|{org}|{external_user_id}",
 where org is the organization the token is for and external_user_id is
 the product's own stable identifier for the person, so every mint for
 one organization resolves the same person to the same account. The
 "stgm_pc|" prefix is reserved: no other provisioning mode may use it.

 Unlike federated accounts, nothing outside Stigmer vouches for the
 person on each request: Stigmer signs its own tokens for them, and the
 service account whose key minted the token stays the admission
 credential while the token lives.

values.name: service_account
values.description:
An organization's own non-person account: the principal its automation
 (a CI job, a script, an integration) acts as, so the automation keeps
 working when the person who set it up leaves.

 Created by an organization admin with createServiceAccount, it belongs to
 that one organization for its whole life, holds one organization role
 (admin, member or viewer, never owner) and acts only through API keys
 the organization's admins create for it. Its keys work only in its
 organization, and deleting it ends every key at once.

 The idp_id uses the composite encoding "stgm_sa|{org}|{random}", where
 org is the owning organization's id and random is drawn at creation, so
 a service account deleted and created again under the same name is a
 new principal that inherits nothing. The "stgm_sa|" prefix is reserved:
 no other provisioning mode may use it, and no sign-in resolves to it.

enumTypes.name: AccessChange
enumTypes.description: AccessChange says what happened to someone's access.

values.name: granted
values.description: Access was given.

values.name: revoked
values.description: Access was taken away.

enumTypes.name: AccessChangeCause
enumTypes.description:
AccessChangeCause says why someone's access changed. A cause is added,
 never renamed or reused.

values.name: grant
values.description: Someone gave a person, a team or a group a role.

values.name: revoke
values.description: Someone took a role away.

values.name: structural
values.description:
The server recorded what creating a resource implies: its creator's
 ownership, or the audience its visibility opens it to.

values.name: organization_access_revoked
values.description: Someone removed a person from the organization.

values.name: left_organization
values.description:
A person left the organization, and the server took away what they
 still held on its resources.

values.name: resource_deleted
values.description: A resource was deleted, and its access with it.

values.name: organization_created
values.description: A person created the organization and became its owner.

values.name: first_sign_in
values.description:
A person signed in for the first time and was given the roles the
 server's membership rules grant.

values.name: role_reconciliation
values.description:
The server gave existing accounts the roles its membership rules would
 have given them.

values.name: operator_ownership
values.description: The server's operator became owner of an organization nobody owned.

values.name: service_account_created
values.description:
An administrator created a service account with its role in the
 organization.

values.name: api_resource_version
values.description: Immutable version record tracking changes to an API resource.

values.name: grant
values.description:
One role given to one principal on one resource. Who holds what on a
 resource is the set of its grants.

values.name: identity_account
values.description: User account in the identity system.

values.name: api_key
values.description: Credential for programmatic API access.

values.name: invitation
values.description: Shareable link for joining an organization with a configurable role.

values.name: federation_issuer
values.description:
An outside issuer whose tokens Stigmer accepts for its own users
 (identity federation): its keys, its audience, and what its tokens get.

values.name: oauth_app
values.description: Registered OAuth application with an external vendor for outbound authentication.

values.name: team
values.description: Named group of an organization's people that access is shared with as one.

values.name: organization
values.description:
The boundary that holds people, Agents, Sessions and secrets
 together; nothing outside it sees them.

 Its id is a minted org_<ulid> that never changes; every organization-scoped
 resource names it by that id (metadata.org). Its slug is unique across the
 server and may change through rename; requests may name the organization
 by either.

values.name: platform
values.description: Singleton platform instance representing the Stigmer deployment.

values.name: agent
values.description: AI assistant with instructions, tools, skills, and a delegation model.

values.name: run
values.description: Single run of an agent within a session, tracking tool calls and responses.

values.name: session
values.description: Conversation thread between a user and an agent.

values.name: skill
values.description: Knowledge resource that provides domain-specific context to an agent.

values.name: channel
values.description:
A way people reach an agent: a chat link or website widget, a Slack
 workspace, or a WhatsApp number.

values.name: channel_app
values.description:
Customer-owned messaging-platform app (e.g. a Slack app) that
 channels can install through instead of the shared platform app.

values.name: routine
values.description:
A saved agent invocation, run on an optional schedule or fired by Run now
 or over the API, acting as its owner.

values.name: memory
values.description: Agent-proposed, user-confirmed fact the platform remembers about a person.

values.name: plugin
values.description:
An installed Agent Plugins package: one thing holding skills, agents,
 hooks and MCP servers, which agents and conversations list whole.

values.name: vault
values.description:
A person's or an organization's box of logins (matched by a tool's
 address) and secrets (matched by name) that runs use.

values.name: score
values.description:
One grade of a finished run: a person's thumbs or a free run-health
 check.

values.name: scoring_rule
values.description:
AI grading switched on for one agent: its sample rate, monthly spending
 limit and judge model.

values.name: eval_run
values.description:
One run of test cases on an agent, or on a plugin on the built-in
 assistant, optionally with and without a plugin.

values.name: eval
values.description:
A set of test cases for an agent: an evals/ folder in Claude Code's
 plugin-eval format, pushed whole.

values.name: environment
values.description:
A named sandbox setup: the packages installed in every sandbox a
 conversation using it runs in, and the hosts it may reach.

values.name: file
values.description:
A file uploaded once and named by its id: given to a conversation with
 a message, held in a conversation's resources, or kept by its uploader.

values.name: plan
values.description:
Catalog entry naming a bundle of entitlements and the terms that buy it.

 Platform-level: a plan belongs to no organization, so it carries no
 authorization scope and no owner. Immutable once created; a change of
 terms is a new Plan and the old one retires.

values.name: subscription
values.description:
An organization's binding to a Plan; at most one active per organization.

 System-created: the payment system drives its lifecycle, so it has no
 owner and grants no roles. Its reads and writes authorize on the
 organization through the billing permissions.

values.name: license
values.description:
A signed grant of entitlements to a self-hosting customer for a term.

 Platform-level: issued by the cloud's operators and verified offline by
 the Enterprise server, so the customer is a value inside the license
 (which may or may not name a cloud organization) and the kind has no
 authorization scope and no owner. Claims are immutable once signed; a
 renewal is a new License.

resourceDescription:
Grant represents a binding between a principal (who), a resource (what),
 and a relation/permission (how).

 A grant gives a specific permission (relation) to a principal on a resource.
 For example: "Grant 'admin' permission to user 'john@example.com' on VPC 'vpc-123'"

 The grant is the source of truth for authorization and is synced to the
 authorization backend (OpenFGA) as FGA tuples.
